patch.value:
Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1460

## Problem
`pm merge install` writes this into the tracked `.gitattributes` fence:
```gitattributes
".agents/pm/**/*.json" merge=pm-json
".agents/pm/extensions/**" -merge
".agents/pm/extensions/.managed-extensions.json" merge=pm-json
```
The source comment (`src/sdk/merge/install.ts`, added in #916) says the intent is an escape hatch: extension package assets should not go through the pm item and stream drivers. But `-merge` does not mean "no custom driver". In gitattributes, **`-merge` (unset) means "treat as binary"**:
- when both branches change an extension file, Git keeps the current branch's version as the tentative result and reports a conflict;
- it writes **no conflict markers**, so the other side's edit can easily be lost, because the file looks clean;
- non-conflicting edits from both sides are not combined either.

What the comment describes is `!merge` (unspecified, meaning Git's built-in 3-way text merge) or an explicit `merge=text`. Either one excludes the files from `pm-json` / `pm-relationship` without making them binary.

## Impact
Any repository that vendors or develops an extension under `.agents/pm/extensions/` (fleet packages do this during development and in packed-consumer tests) gets binary-merge semantics on text sources. A code-review bot flagged it on a downstream PR (unbraind/pm-lint#6). Consumers cannot fix it locally: the fence is generated, and `pm health` reports any edit as `merge_fence_drift`.

## Proposal
1. Emit `".agents/pm/extensions/**" merge=text` (or `!merge`) instead of `-merge`, and keep the later `merge=pm-json` override for `.managed-extensions.json`.
2. Bump the fence version marker so `pm merge install` / health refresh existing fences.
3. Add a test that merges two branches each editing a different line of an extension source file: expect a clean text merge. Editing the same line should produce standard conflict markers.


Implementation intent

Correct generated extension asset merge semantics without sending package content to tracker drivers or selecting binary merge for text sources.
GH-1460: Merge extension assets as ordinary Git files while preserving tracker drivers
Correct generated extension asset merge semantics without sending package content to tracker drivers or selecting binary merge for text sources.

Prove real native Git non-overlapping and conflicting extension merges; Keep managed inventory and contributed item drivers intact; Refresh installed fences without reverting sibling or older-version safety

Non-overlapping extension text edits merge cleanly, overlapping edits retain standard conflict markers and binary assets remain protected by native Git behavior, while the managed registry retains pm-json.
